# Phase Three — Route-Wide Mobile Quality Execution Plan

## Production-first rule for this discovered mission
No production mutation is justified yet. The first implementation is a browser quality instrument because the unknown is whether route-wide defects exist. If the instrument reveals defects, then production fixes will be written first in the repair pass, followed by rerun tests.

## Files to create

### `tests/BrowserSurfaceQualityInspector.mjs`
A focused CDP DOM inspector under 120 lines. It receives the active route ID and returns objective evidence: panel geometry, document overflow, horizontal escape samples, loose direct-text samples, invisible text samples, and undersized ordinary interactive samples.

### `tests/BrowserRouteQualityJourney.mjs`
A focused orchestrator under 120 lines. It imports live `ROUTES`, iterates all twelve route IDs, sets the hash without invoking destructive controls, waits for active panel visibility, invokes the inspector, and asserts zero objective defects with route-specific messages.

## Existing file to rewrite only after focused audit proves stable
### `tests/browserSmoke.test.mjs`
If the route-wide journey works deterministically, rewrite the whole smoke file to invoke it during the existing 390px fixture session. Keep the file below 120 lines. Do not modify the normal unit-test package chain unless the browser suite remains the correct owner.

## Objective quality rules
1. Active panel has positive width/height.
2. Document horizontal overflow <= 1px rounding tolerance.
3. Visible route descendants do not escape viewport horizontally by >1px unless their computed overflow contract explicitly contains internal scrolling.
4. Meaningful direct text nodes under generic DIV/SECTION/ARTICLE/LI containers are allowed only when the parent itself is a styled/semantic vessel: class/id present plus visible typography or surface treatment.
5. Visible text-bearing elements must have nontransparent color and positive font size/line height.
6. Ordinary visible buttons/anchors/selects/inputs/textarea should have practical mobile height; exceptions include checkbox/radio/range/file controls and controls explicitly styled as compact inline utilities.
7. Audit never clicks posting, deletion, membership, privacy mutation, or communication-send controls.
8. Persistent mobile Create and dock remain present while each route is inspected, so global collisions remain visible to document overflow.

## Repair protocol if failures appear
For every failing route: record exact evidence → read exact template/controller/style owner → add defect to REMAINING_WORK → rewrite whole production file(s) with modular split if necessary → reread source → rerun focused route audit → run full `npm run test:all`.

## Verification and closure
- node-check new browser modules;
- line-count all new/touched files;
- run route-wide browser journey alone;
- integrate it into browser smoke only after deterministic pass;
- rerun `npm run test:all`;
- update final verification and REMAINING_WORK with actual route results.

The Awtsmoos is not served by invented defects; Awtsmoos.com will ask each of the twelve chambers to stand before living Chrome. What spills will be repaired, what is already clothed will be left whole, and the final word will come from evidence.
